1. Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited (e.g. TJC, CHAP, etc.).

The Applicant, AdviniaCare Newport, LLC (“New Operator” or “Applicant”), seeks Change in
Effective Control (“CEC”) approval for the acquisition of Heatherwood Rehabilitation & Health
Care Center (“Heatherwood” or the “Facility”), a 114 Bed nursing facility located at 398 Bellevue
Avenue in Newport, RI (the “Heatherwood Property”). Heatherwood RI LLC (“Current Operator”)
currently operates the Facility. Bellevue Ave, LLC (the “New Real Estate Owner”) seeks CEC
approval for the purchase of the Heatherwood Property.

The Transaction

The Applicant will acquire the operations of the Facility pursuant to an Operations Transfer
Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View LLC, Heatherwood RI LLC, Waterview RI SNF
LLC, Summit RI SNF LLC, and Oakland Grove Associates, L.P., (collectively, “Current Operators”)
collectively, as Sellers and AdviniaCare Newport, LLC, AdviniaCare Oakland Grove, LLC,
AdviniaCare Orchard, LLC, AdviniaCare Summit Commons, LLC, and AdviniaCare Waterview
Villas, LLC (collectively, “New Operators”), collectively, as Purchasers, dated as of August 7, 2025
(the “OTA”) (Tab 14). In addition to this Facility, four affiliated entities of the Applicant will acquire
the operations of four affiliated facilities of the Current Operator – Orchard View Manor, Waterview
Villa Rehabilitation & Skilled Care Center, Summit Commons Rehabilitation & Health Center, and
Oakland Grove Health Care Center (collectively, the “Affiliated Facilities”).

Pursuant to a Asset Purchase Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View Landlord LLC,
Heatherwood Landlord LLC, Waterview RI Landlord LLC, Summit RI Landlord LLC, and
Oakland Grove Landlord, LLC (collectively, “Current Real Estate Owners”), collectively, as Sellers
and Bellevue Ave, LLC, Cumberland Hill, LLC, Tripps Lane, LLC, 99 Hillside, LLC and South
Broadway, LLC dated as of Augst 7, 2025 (the “APA”) (Tab 14), the New Real Estate Owner will
acquire the real estate of the Facility. Pursuant to the APA, four affiliated entities of the Applicant
will acquire the real estate of the Affiliated Facilities. Pursuant to a lease agreement (Tab 24), the
New Operator will lease the Heatherwood Property from the New Real Estate Owner.

The purchase price for Facility and Affiliated Facilities is $75,000,000. The Applicant will finance the
Proposed Transaction with 80% debt ($50,000,000, conventional mortgage) and 20% equity
($25,000,000).

The Applicant

The Applicant’s sole member is RI 5 Holdco Op, LLC, (“RI 5 Holdco Op”) a Rhode Island limited
liability company. The corporate manager of the Applicant is AdviniaCare, LLC. The members of
RI 5 Holdco Op are: RI 5 Investor Group, LLC (25.50%), Yosef Meystel Delta Trust (18.50%), David
A. Berkowitz Delta Trust (18.50%), Benjamin Berkowitz Revocable Trust (18.50%), Moshe Braun




                                                    1

===== PAGE 4 =====
(10%), Leah Braun Trust (5%), Brian Goldfarb (2%), Moriel Hamui (1%), and Frederick S. Frankel
Trust (1%). The corporate manager of RI 5 Holdco is AdviniaCare, LLC (“AdviniaCare”).

The New Real Estate Owner’s sole member is RI 5 Holdco Prop, LLC (“RI 5 Holco Prop”). The New
Real Estate Owner’s corporate manager is Pointe Property, LLC. RI 5 Holdco Prop members are:
RI 5 Investor Group, LLC (25%), Yosef Meystel Delta Trust (18.50%), David A. Berkowitz Delta
Trust (18.50%), Benjamin Berkowitz Revocable Trust (18.50%), Moshe Braun (10%), Leah Braun
Trust (5%), Brian Goldfarb (2%), Moriel Hamui (1%), and Frederick S. Frankel Trust (1%).

Yosef Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz – the principals of the Applicant – through an
affiliated entity, own and operate AdviniaCare Pawtucket and AdviniaCare Providence. The Rhode
Island Department of Health (“RIDOH”) approved the CEC applications for the operations of those
facilities on January 31, 2025. In fact, an affiliated entity began providing management services at
those facilities pursuant to a RIDOH-approved management agreement since February of 2023. Since
their management of those facilities, the annual survey outcomes for the facilities significantly
improved, the operators prioritized decreasing turnover in key positions, the operators were able to
eliminate all agency staff and worked collaboratively with the unions in those facilities, and have
infused capital into the facilities. The Applicant will provide the same dedication to this Facility upon
approval of the CEC Application.

Moreover, Mr. Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz own and/or operate a total of 111
licensed facilities in 8 states.

Ben Berkowitz is an owner operator of 15 nursing facilities and senior housing facilities in Florida
and Massachusetts, as well as an investor in facilities in other states. Specifically, he is the Chief
Executive Officer of Pointe Group Care, LLC (“PGC”), which is headquartered in Massachusetts.
PGC employs staff focusing on operations, accounting, clinical, business development, technology
and accounts receivable and payable. PCG takes pride in providing high quality short-term
rehabilitation, nursing, and long-term care.

David Berkowitz and Yosef Meystel are the founders of Aperion Care, Inc. (“Aperion Care”).
Aperion Care is an administrative and management company firm that partners with geriatric
healthcare facilities. It specifically provides management services to skilled nursing facilities and
assisted living communities throughout Illinois and Indiana. Mr. Meystel began his career in
healthcare as an Assistant Administrator at Brightview Care Center in Chicago, Illinois. Following
Brightview, Mr. Meystel was the Administrator for EMI/EKS Management, where he became the
Administrator for Emerald Park Health Care Center. In 2006, Mr. Meystel founded YAM
Management, LLC and in 2014 formed Aperion Care, Inc., for which he serves as a board member
and shareholder. Aperion Care and PCG are now subsidiaries of the Kesser Group.

David Berkowitz serves as the President of Aperion Care, Inc., as well as a director and a shareholder.
He began his career in healthcare in 2002 as an administrator in training at Sebos Nursing & Rehab.
David Berkowitz then served as an administrator at a number of other skilled nursing facilities. He
has ownership interest in the real estate and/or operating entities of many skilled nursing facilities
located throughout Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Massachusetts, Florida and Kansas.

experience in multi-facility operations, stabilizing workforces, ensuring compliance, and driving

Massachusetts and Rhode Island – overseeing the 8 facilities in the area.

11. Please provide a concise description of the services currently offered by the licensed entity and
identify any services that will be added, terminated, expanded, or reduced and state the reasons therefore:

Heatherwood offers a full range of nursing care and social services. It also provides specialty
programs including rehabilitation therapy programs (physical, occupational and speech language),
health management (nutrition, diabetes care, wound care), recreational therapy, and support
services. There are no plans to change any of the current services offered.

21.   Please identify any planned actions of the applicant to reduce, limit, or contain health care costs and
improve the efficiency with which health care services are delivered to the citizens of this state.

The Applicant will strive to deliver high quality, cost-effective health care services to all of its patients.
In order to do so, it will strive to hire skilled health care professionals and implement its Quality
Assurance Policy, as set forth in response to Question 22 below. Additionally, the Applicant aims to
provide better access to post-acute care services, with better outcomes, and at lower costs to its
patients.

23. Please provide a detailed description about the amount and source of the equity and debt commitment
for this transaction. (NOTE: If debt is contemplated as part of the financing, please complete Appendix E).
Additionally, please demonstrate the following:

A. The immediate and long-term financial feasibility of the proposed financing plan;

As set forth in Tab C3, the New Operator’s principals have the financial ability to consummate the
purchase and operate the Facility. The current financing plan involves a three year conventional
mortgage. As set forth in Appendix A, the Applicant projects that, following the improvements to the
Facility and Affiliated Facility’s operations, they will generate the income for the financing payments.
As a result, the financing is feasible both immediately and long-term given the capability of the New
Operator’s principals.

B. The relative availability of funds for capital and operating needs; and

The New Operator has access to sufficient funds for capital and operating needs as evidenced by the
financial projections in Appendix A, the written certification from Rachel Stein, CPA at Roth &
Company, and the bank account statements (both at Appendix C3), confirming that the Applicants
have the financial capability to acquire and safely operate five nursing homes in Rhode Island.

C. The applicant’s financial capability.

The Applicant is a newly-formed entity for the Proposed Transaction. However, the New Operator
and its parent’s members have access to sufficient funds for all operating needs, reflected by its
financial capability to operate the facility. Please see the written certification from Rachel Stein, CPA
at Roth & Company and the bank account statement.

                                           Appendix C (CONT.)

5.      Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and operational
policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services, and accommodations, and a
sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the proposal would advance these areas:

a.     Resident’s physical environment:

      i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

       The facility offers both shared and private accommodations for residents. Common areas are
       available for interaction with other residents when preferred.

     ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

       The facility offers rooms with modern décor. The residential rooms can be decorated with the
       residents’ personal belongings to promote a more familiar and comfortable environment.

     iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s), laundry,
         activities;

       Laundry service is provided. The Applicant will offer a diverse nutritious menu that caters to
       personal preference, allergy needs, religious beliefs, and physical comfort. Group activities
       are available daily.

     iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and gardening);

       The facility offers many outdoor spaces, including, for example, a patio area.

b.     Resident-centered systems of care:

      i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and negotiated risk;

       The Facility offers a home-like and autonomous environment, while still maintaining
       appropriate physical security systems. The Applicant will ensure that the physical security
       system, including wander management systems on main exits and alarms on egress doors are
       current and operational.

     ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);

       The Applicant works with residents to schedule their preferred times for waking, bathing, and
       going to bed. The residents are also able to schedule their daily activities throughout the day.

     iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);




                                                       24

===== PAGE 27 =====
       The Applicant encourages the residents to provide their preferred dining time and location,
       as well as their meal preferences. Applicant will provide an alternate meal choice and make
       snacks available throughout the day. The dietary staff also ensures that residents with
       restrictive diets are able to enjoy an assortment of different meals.

     iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

       As set forth above, the structured recreational program includes a wide variety of activities
       for residents. The Applicant encourages resident feedback on those activities so that they can
       consistently improve and update the offerings. Residents may also participate in their own
       self-directed activities and always have access to television, books, movies, card games,
       beauty/barber salon and religious services for many denominations.

c.     Workforce administration:

      i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident services and
        foster relationship building?

       The Applicant will ensure that the facility maintains appropriate staffing ratios on all shifts
       and in all units. Staffing assignments take into account staff capabilities and specific needs of
       residents. In order to ensure the appropriate coverage, the Applicant continuously monitors
       the census and the residents’ conditions.

     ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g. Registered nurses,
        Licensed Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

       The Applicant will minimize staff turnover through job satisfaction and financial incentives.
       Staff is encouraged to recognize the significant role that they play in each residents’ life. Any
       changes in staffing are discussed with the residents before implementation.

1.     Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited (e.g. TJC, CHAP, etc.).

The Applicant, AdviniaCare Oakland Grove, LLC (“New Operator” or “Applicant”), seeks Change
in Effective Control (“CEC”) approval for the acquisition of Oakland Grove Health Care Center
(“Oakland Grove” or the “Facility”), a 178 Bed nursing facility located at 560 Cumberland Hill Road
in Woonsocket, RI (the “Oakland Grove Property”). Oakland Grove Associates LP (“Current
Operator”) currently operates the Facility. Cumberland Hill, LLC (the “New Real Estate Owner”)
seeks CEC approval for the purchase of the Oakland Grove Property.

The Transaction

The Applicant will acquire the operations of the Facility pursuant to an Operations Transfer
Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View LLC, Heatherwood RI LLC, Waterview RI SNF
LLC, Summit RI SNF LLC, and Oakland Grove Associates, L.P., (collectively, “Current Operators”)
collectively, as Sellers and AdviniaCare Newport, LLC, AdviniaCare Oakland Grove, LLC,
AdviniaCare Orchard, LLC, AdviniaCare Summit Commons, LLC, and AdviniaCare Waterview
Villas, LLC (collectively, “New Operators”), collectively, as Purchasers, dated as of August 7, 2025
(the “OTA”) (Tab 14). In addition to this Facility, four affiliated entities of the Applicant will acquire
the operations of four affiliated facilities of the Current Operator – Heatherwood Rehabilitation and
Health Care Center, Waterview Villa Rehabilitation & Skilled Care Center, Summit Commons
Rehabilitation & Health Center, and Orchard View Manor Rehabilitation & Nursing Center
(collectively, the “Affiliated Facilities”).

Pursuant to a Asset Purchase Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View Landlord LLC,
Heatherwood Landlord LLC, Waterview RI Landlord LLC, Summit RI Landlord LLC, and
Oakland Grove Landlord, LLC (collectively, “Current Real Estate Owners”), collectively, as Sellers
and Bellevue Ave, LLC, Cumberland Hill, LLC, Tripps Lane, LLC, 99 Hillside, LLC and South
Broadway, LLC dated as of Augst 7, 2025 (the “APA”) (Tab 14), the New Real Estate Owner will
acquire the real estate of the Facility. Pursuant to the APA, four affiliated entities of the Applicant
will acquire the real estate of the Affiliated Facilities. Pursuant to a lease agreement (Tab 24), the
New Operator will lease the Oakland Grove Property from the New Real Estate Owner.

The purchase price for Facility and Affiliated Facilities is $75,000,000. The Applicant will finance the
Proposed Transaction with 80% debt ($50,000,000, conventional mortgage) and 20% equity
($25,000,000).

The Applicant

The Applicant’s sole member is RI 5 Holdco Op, LLC, (“RI 5 Holdco Op”) a Rhode Island limited
liability company. The corporate manager of the Applicant is AdviniaCare, LLC. The members of
RI 5 Holdco Op are: RI 5 Investor Group, LLC (25.50%), Yosef Meystel Delta Trust (18.50%), David
A. Berkowitz Delta Trust (18.50%), Benjamin Berkowitz Revocable Trust (18.50%), Moshe Braun

Yosef Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz – the principals of the Applicant – through an
affiliated entity, own and operate AdviniaCare Pawtucket and AdviniaCare Providence. The Rhode
Island Department of Health (“RIDOH”) approved the CEC applications for the operations of those
facilities on January 31, 2025. In fact, an affiliated entity began providing management services at
those facilities pursuant to a RIDOH-approved management agreement since February of 2023. Since
their management of those facilities, the annual survey outcomes for the facilities significantly
improved, the operators prioritized decreasing turnover in key positions, the operators were able to

approval of the CEC Application.

Moreover, Mr. Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz own and/or operate a total of 111
licensed facilities in 8 states.

Ben Berkowitz is an owner operator of 11 nursing facilities and senior housing facilities in Florida
and Massachusetts, as well as an investor in facilities in other states. Specifically, he is the Chief
Executive Officer of Pointe Group Care, LLC (“PGC”), which is headquartered in Massachusetts.
PGC employs staff focusing on operations, accounting, clinical, business development, technology
and accounts receivable and payable. PCG takes pride in providing high quality short-term
rehabilitation, nursing, and long-term care.

David Berkowitz and Yosef Meystel are the founders of Aperion Care, Inc. (“Aperion Care”).
Aperion Care is an administrative and management company firm that partners with geriatric
healthcare facilities. It specifically provides management services to skilled nursing facilities and
assisted living communities throughout Illinois and Indiana. Mr. Meystel began his career in
healthcare as an Assistant Administrator at Brightview Care Center in Chicago, Illinois. Following
Brightview, Mr. Meystel was the Administrator for EMI/EKS Management, where he became the
Administrator for Emerald Park Health Care Center. In 2006, Mr. Meystel founded YAM
Management, LLC and in 2014 formed Aperion Care, Inc., for which he serves as a board member
and shareholder. Aperion Care and PCG are now subsidiaries of the Kesser Group.

David Berkowitz serves as the President of Aperion Care, Inc., as well as a director and a shareholder.

has ownership interest in the real estate and/or operating entities of many skilled nursing facilities

a.     Resident’s physical environment:

      i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

       The facility offers both shared and private accommodations for residents. Common areas are
       available for interaction with other residents when preferred.

     ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

       The facility offers rooms with modern décor. The residential rooms can be decorated with the
       residents’ personal belongings to promote a more familiar and comfortable environment.

     iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s), laundry,
         activities;

       Laundry service is provided. The Applicant will offer a diverse nutritious menu that caters to
       personal preference, allergy needs, religious beliefs, and physical comfort. Group activities
       are available daily.

     iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and gardening);

       The facility offers many outdoor spaces, including, for example, a patio area.

b.     Resident-centered systems of care:

      i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and negotiated risk;

       The Facility offers a home-like and autonomous environment, while still maintaining
       appropriate physical security systems. The Applicant will ensure that the physical security
       system, including wander management systems on main exits and alarms on egress doors are
       current and operational.

     ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);

       The Applicant works with residents to schedule their preferred times for waking, bathing, and
       going to bed. The residents are also able to schedule their daily activities throughout the day.

     iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);




                                                       24

===== PAGE 61 =====
       The Applicant encourages the residents to provide their preferred dining time and location,
       as well as their meal preferences. Applicant will provide an alternate meal choice and make
       snacks available throughout the day. The dietary staff also ensures that residents with
       restrictive diets are able to enjoy an assortment of different meals.

     iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

       As set forth above, the structured recreational program includes a wide variety of activities
       for residents. The Applicant encourages resident feedback on those activities so that they can
       consistently improve and update the offerings. Residents may also participate in their own
       self-directed activities and always have access to television, books, movies, card games,
       beauty/barber salon and religious services for many denominations.

c.     Workforce administration:

      i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident services and
        foster relationship building?

       The Applicant will ensure that the facility maintains appropriate staffing ratios on all shifts
       and in all units. Staffing assignments take into account staff capabilities and specific needs of
       residents. In order to ensure the appropriate coverage, the Applicant continuously monitors
       the census and the residents’ conditions.

     ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g. Registered nurses,
        Licensed Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

       The Applicant will minimize staff turnover through job satisfaction and financial incentives.
       Staff is encouraged to recognize the significant role that they play in each residents’ life. Any
       changes in staffing are discussed with the residents before implementation.

1.      Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited (e.g. TJC, CHAP, etc.).

The Applicant, AdviniaCare Orchard, LLC (“New Operator” or “Applicant”), seeks Change in
Effective Control (“CEC”) approval for the acquisition of Orchard View Manor Rehabilitation &
Nursing Center (“Orchard View” or the “Facility”), a 166 Bed nursing facility located at 135 Tripps
Lane, in East Providence, RI (the “Tripps Lane Property”). Athena Orchard View LLC (“Current
Operator”) currently operates the Facility. Tripps Lane, LLC (the “New Real Estate Owner”) seeks
CEC approval for the purchase of the Tripps Lane Property.

The Transaction

The Applicant will acquire the operations of the Facility pursuant to an Operations Transfer
Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View LLC, Heatherwood RI LLC, Waterview RI SNF
LLC, Summit RI SNF LLC, and Oakland Grove Associates, L.P., (collectively, “Current Operators”)
collectively, as Sellers and AdviniaCare Newport, LLC, AdviniaCare Oakland Grove, LLC,
AdviniaCare Orchard, LLC, AdviniaCare Summit Commons, LLC, and AdviniaCare Waterview
Villas, LLC (collectively, “New Operators”), collectively, as Purchasers, dated as of August 7, 2025
(the “OTA”) (Tab 14). In addition to this Facility, four affiliated entities of the Applicant will acquire
the operations of four affiliated facilities of the Current Operator – Heatherwood Rehabilitation and
Health Care Center, Waterview Villa Rehabilitation & Skilled Care Center, Summit Commons
Rehabilitation & Health Center, and Oakland Grove Health Care Center (collectively, the “Affiliated
Facilities”).

Pursuant to a Asset Purchase Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View Landlord LLC,
Heatherwood Landlord LLC, Waterview RI Landlord LLC, Summit RI Landlord LLC, and
Oakland Grove Landlord, LLC (collectively, “Current Real Estate Owners”), collectively, as Sellers
and Bellevue Ave, LLC, Cumberland Hill, LLC, Tripps Lane, LLC, 99 Hillside, LLC and South
Broadway, LLC dated as of Augst 7, 2025 (the “APA”) (Tab 14), the “New Real Estate Owner will
acquire the real estate of the Facility. Pursuant to the APA, four affiliated entities of the Applicant
will acquire the real estate of the Affiliated Facilities. Pursuant to a lease agreement (Tab 24), the
New Operator will lease the Tripps Lane Property from the New Real Estate Owner.

The purchase price for Facility and Affiliated Facilities is $75,000,000. The Applicant will finance the
Proposed Transaction with 80% debt ($50,000,000, conventional mortgage) and 20% equity
($25,000,000).

                                           Appendix C (CONT.)

5.      Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and operational
policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services, and accommodations, and a
sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the proposal would advance these areas:

a.     Resident’s physical environment:

      i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

       The facility offers both shared and private accommodations for residents. Common areas are
       available for interaction with other residents when preferred.

     ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

       The facility offers rooms with modern décor. The residential rooms can be decorated with the
       residents’ personal belongings to promote a more familiar and comfortable environment.

     iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s), laundry,
         activities;

       Laundry service is provided. The Applicant will offer a diverse nutritious menu that caters to
       personal preference, allergy needs, religious beliefs, and physical comfort. Group activities
       are available daily.

     iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and gardening);

       The facility offers many outdoor spaces, including, for example, a patio area.

b.     Resident-centered systems of care:

      i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and negotiated risk;

       The Facility offers a home-like and autonomous environment, while still maintaining
       appropriate physical security systems. The Applicant will ensure that the physical security
       system, including wander management systems on main exits and alarms on egress doors are
       current and operational.

     ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);

       The Applicant works with residents to schedule their preferred times for waking, bathing, and
       going to bed. The residents are also able to schedule their daily activities throughout the day.

     iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);




                                                       24

===== PAGE 95 =====
       The Applicant encourages the residents to provide their preferred dining time and location,
       as well as their meal preferences. Applicant will provide an alternate meal choice and make
       snacks available throughout the day. The dietary staff also ensures that residents with
       restrictive diets are able to enjoy an assortment of different meals.

     iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

       As set forth above, the structured recreational program includes a wide variety of activities
       for residents. The Applicant encourages resident feedback on those activities so that they can
       consistently improve and update the offerings. Residents may also participate in their own
       self-directed activities and always have access to television, books, movies, card games,
       beauty/barber salon and religious services for many denominations.

c.     Workforce administration:

      i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident services and
        foster relationship building?

       The Applicant will ensure that the facility maintains appropriate staffing ratios on all shifts
       and in all units. Staffing assignments take into account staff capabilities and specific needs of
       residents. In order to ensure the appropriate coverage, the Applicant continuously monitors
       the census and the residents’ conditions.

     ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g. Registered nurses,
        Licensed Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

       The Applicant will minimize staff turnover through job satisfaction and financial incentives.
       Staff is encouraged to recognize the significant role that they play in each residents’ life. Any
       changes in staffing are discussed with the residents before implementation.

1. Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited (e.g. TJC, CHAP, etc.).

The Applicant, AdviniaCare Summit Commons, LLC (“New Operator” or “Applicant”), seeks
Change in Effective Control (“CEC”) approval for the acquisition of Summit Commons
Rehabilitation & Health Care Center (“Summit Commons” or the “Facility”), a 165 Bed nursing
facility located at 99 Hillside Ave in Providence, RI (the “Hillside Property”). Summit RI SNF, LLC
(“Current Operator”) currently operates the Facility. 99 Hillside, LLC (the “New Real Estate
Owner”) seeks CEC approval for the purchase of the Hillside Property.

The Transaction

The Applicant will acquire the operations of the Facility pursuant to an Operations Transfer
Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View LLC, Heatherwood RI LLC, Waterview RI SNF
LLC, Summit RI SNF LLC, and Oakland Grove Associates, L.P., (collectively, “Current Operators”)
collectively, as Sellers and AdviniaCare Newport, LLC, AdviniaCare Oakland Grove, LLC,
AdviniaCare Orchard, LLC, AdviniaCare Summit Commons, LLC, and AdviniaCare Waterview
Villas, LLC (collectively, “New Operators”), collectively, as Purchasers, dated as of August 7, 2025
(the “OTA”) (Tab 14). In addition to this Facility, four affiliated entities of the Applicant will acquire
the operations of four affiliated facilities of the Current Operator – Heatherwood Rehabilitation and
Health Care Center, Waterview Villa Rehabilitation & Skilled Care Center, Orchard View Manor
Rehabilitation & Nursing Center, and Oakland Grove Health Care Center (collectively, the
“Affiliated Facilities”).

Pursuant to a Asset Purchase Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View Landlord LLC,
Heatherwood Landlord LLC, Waterview RI Landlord LLC, Summit RI Landlord LLC, and
Oakland Grove Landlord, LLC (collectively, “Current Real Estate Owners”), collectively, as Sellers
and Bellevue Ave, LLC, Cumberland Hill, LLC, Tripps Lane, LLC, 99 Hillside, LLC and South
Broadway, LLC dated as of Augst 7, 2025 (the “APA”) (Tab 14), the New Real Estate Owner will
acquire the real estate of the Facility. Pursuant to the APA, four affiliated entities of the Applicant
will acquire the real estate of the Affiliated Facilities. Pursuant to a lease agreement (Tab 24), the
New Operator will lease the Hillside Property from the New Real Estate Owner.

The purchase price for Facility and Affiliated Facilities is $75,000,000. The Applicant will finance the
Proposed Transaction with 80% debt ($50,000,000, conventional mortgage) and 20% equity
($25,000,000).

The Applicant

The Applicant’s sole member is RI 5 Holdco Op, LLC, (“RI 5 Holdco Op”) a Rhode Island limited
liability company. The corporate manager of the Applicant is AdviniaCare, LLC. The members of
RI 5 Holdco Op are: RI 5 Investor Group, LLC (25.50%), Yosef Meystel Delta Trust (18.50%), David
A. Berkowitz Delta Trust (18.50%), Benjamin Berkowitz Revocable Trust (18.50%), Moshe Braun

(10%), Leah Braun Trust (5%), Brian Goldfarb (2%), Moriel Hamui (1%), and Frederick S. Frankel
Trust (1%). The corporate manager of RI 5 Holdco is AdviniaCare, LLC (“AdviniaCare”).

The New Real Estate Owner’s sole member is RI 5 Holdco Prop, LLC (“RI 5 Holco Prop”). The New
Real Estate Owner’s corporate manager is Pointe Property, LLC. RI 5 Holdco Prop members are:
RI 5 Investor Group, LLC (25%), Yosef Meystel Delta Trust (18.50%), David A. Berkowitz Delta

Yosef Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz – the principals of the Applicant – through an

facilities on January 31, 2025. In fact, an affiliated entity began providing management services at
those facilities pursuant to a RIDOH-approved management agreement since February of 2023. Since
their management of those facilities, the annual survey outcomes for the facilities significantly
improved, the operators prioritized decreasing turnover in key positions, the operators were able to
eliminate all agency staff and worked collaboratively with the unions in those facilities, and have
infused capital into the facilities. The Applicant will provide the same dedication to this Facility upon
approval of the CEC Application.

Moreover, Mr. Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz own and/or operate a total of 111
licensed facilities in 8 states.

Ben Berkowitz is an owner operator of 11 nursing facilities and senior housing facilities in Florida
and Massachusetts, as well as an investor in facilities in other states. Specifically, he is the Chief
Executive Officer of Pointe Group Care, LLC (“PGC”), which is headquartered in Massachusetts.
PGC employs staff focusing on operations, accounting, clinical, business development, technology
and accounts receivable and payable. PCG takes pride in providing high quality short-term
rehabilitation, nursing, and long-term care.

David Berkowitz and Yosef Meystel are the founders of Aperion Care, Inc. (“Aperion Care”).
Aperion Care is an administrative and management company firm that partners with geriatric
healthcare facilities. It specifically provides management services to skilled nursing facilities and
assisted living communities throughout Illinois and Indiana. Mr. Meystel began his career in
healthcare as an Assistant Administrator at Brightview Care Center in Chicago, Illinois. Following
Brightview, Mr. Meystel was the Administrator for EMI/EKS Management, where he became the
Administrator for Emerald Park Health Care Center. In 2006, Mr. Meystel founded YAM
Management, LLC and in 2014 formed Aperion Care, Inc., for which he serves as a board member
and shareholder. Aperion Care and PCG are now subsidiaries of the Kesser Group.

David Berkowitz serves as the President of Aperion Care, Inc., as well as a director and a shareholder.
He began his career in healthcare in 2002 as an administrator in training at Sebos Nursing & Rehab.
David Berkowitz then served as an administrator at a number of other skilled nursing facilities. He
has ownership interest in the real estate and/or operating entities of many skilled nursing facilities
located throughout Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Massachusetts, Florida and Kansas.

                                           Appendix C (CONT.)

5.     Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and
operational policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services, and
accommodations, and a sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the proposal
would advance these areas:

a.     Resident’s physical environment:

      i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

       The facility offers both shared and private accommodations for residents. Common areas
       are available for interaction with other residents when preferred.

     ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

       The facility offers rooms with modern décor. The residential rooms can be decorated with
       the residents’ personal belongings to promote a more familiar and comfortable environment.

     iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s), laundry,
         activities;

       Laundry service is provided. The Applicant will offer a diverse nutritious menu that caters
       to personal preference, allergy needs, religious beliefs, and physical comfort. Group activities
       are available daily.

     iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and gardening);

       The facility offers many outdoor spaces, including, for example, a patio area.

b.     Resident-centered systems of care:

      i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and negotiated risk;

       The Facility offers a home-like and autonomous environment, while still maintaining
       appropriate physical security systems. The Applicant will ensure that the physical security
       system, including wander management systems on main exits and alarms on egress doors are
       current and operational.

     ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);

       The Applicant works with residents to schedule their preferred times for waking, bathing,
       and going to bed. The residents are also able to schedule their daily activities throughout the
       day.

     iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);


                                                       24

===== PAGE 129 =====
       The Applicant encourages the residents to provide their preferred dining time and location,
       as well as their meal preferences. Applicant will provide an alternate meal choice and make
       snacks available throughout the day. The dietary staff also ensures that residents with
       restrictive diets are able to enjoy an assortment of different meals.

     iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

       As set forth above, the structured recreational program includes a wide variety of activities
       for residents. The Applicant encourages resident feedback on those activities so that they can
       consistently improve and update the offerings. Residents may also participate in their own
       self-directed activities and always have access to television, books, movies, card games,
       beauty/barber salon and religious services for many denominations.

c.     Workforce administration:

      i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident services and
        foster relationship building?

       The Applicant will ensure that the facility maintains appropriate staffing ratios on all shifts
       and in all units. Staffing assignments take into account staff capabilities and specific needs of
       residents. In order to ensure the appropriate coverage, the Applicant continuously monitors
       the census and the residents’ conditions.

     ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g. Registered nurses,
        Licensed Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

       The Applicant will minimize staff turnover through job satisfaction and financial incentives.
       Staff is encouraged to recognize the significant role that they play in each residents’ life. Any
       changes in staffing are discussed with the residents before implementation.

1.    Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited (e.g. TJC, CHAP, etc.).

The Applicant, AdviniaCare Waterview Villas, LLC (“New Operator” or “Applicant”), seeks Change
in Effective Control (“CEC”) approval for the acquisition of Waterview Villa Rehabilitation
(“Waterview Villa” or the “Facility”), a 132 Bed nursing facility located at 1275 S. Broadway in East
Providence, RI (the “Waterview Property”). Waterview RI SNF, LLC (“Current Operator”)
currently operates the Facility. South Broadway, LLC (the “New Real Estate Owner”) seeks CEC
approval for the purchase of the Waterview Property.

The Transaction

The Applicant will acquire the operations of the Facility pursuant to an Operations Transfer
Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View LLC, Heatherwood RI LLC, Waterview RI SNF
LLC, Summit RI SNF LLC, and Oakland Grove Associates, L.P., (collectively, “Current Operators”)
collectively, as Sellers and AdviniaCare Newport, LLC, AdviniaCare Oakland Grove, LLC,
AdviniaCare Orchard, LLC, AdviniaCare Summit Commons, LLC, and AdviniaCare Waterview
Villas, LLC (collectively, “New Operators”), collectively, as Purchasers, dated as of August 7, 2025
(the “OTA”) (Tab 14). In addition to this Facility, four affiliated entities of the Applicant will acquire
the operations of four affiliated facilities of the Current Operator – Heatherwood Rehabilitation and
Health Care Center, Summit Commons Rehabilitation & Health Care Center, Orchard View Manor
Rehabilitation & Nursing Center, and Oakland Grove Health Care Center (collectively, the
“Affiliated Facilities”).

Pursuant to a Asset Purchase Agreement by and between Athena Orchard View Landlord LLC,
Heatherwood Landlord LLC, Waterview RI Landlord LLC, Summit RI Landlord LLC, and
Oakland Grove Landlord, LLC (collectively, “Current Real Estate Owners”), collectively, as Sellers
and Bellevue Ave, LLC, Cumberland Hill, LLC, Tripps Lane, LLC, 99 Hillside, LLC and South
Broadway, LLC dated as of Augst 7, 2025 (the “APA”) (Tab 14), the New Real Estate Owner will
acquire the real estate of the Facility. Pursuant to the APA, four affiliated entities of the Applicant
will acquire the real estate of the Affiliated Facilities. Pursuant to a lease agreement (Tab 24), the
New Operator will lease the Waterview Property from the New Real Estate Owner.

The purchase price for Facility and Affiliated Facilities is $75,000,000. The Applicant will finance the
Proposed Transaction with 80% debt ($50,000,000, conventional mortgage) and 20% equity
($25,000,000).

The Applicant

The Applicant’s sole member is RI 5 Holdco Op, LLC, (“RI 5 Holdco Op”) a Rhode Island limited
liability company. The corporate manager of the Applicant is AdviniaCare, LLC. The members of
RI 5 Holdco Op are: RI 5 Investor Group, LLC (25.50%), Yosef Meystel Delta Trust (18.50%), David
A. Berkowitz Delta Trust (18.50%), Benjamin Berkowitz Revocable Trust (18.50%), Moshe Braun

The New Real Estate Owner’s sole member is RI 5 Holdco Prop, LLC (“RI 5 Holco Prop”). The New
Real Estate Owner’s corporate manager is Pointe Property, LLC. RI 5 Holdco Prop members are:
RI 5 Investor Group, LLC (25%), Yosef Meystel Delta Trust (18.50%), David A. Berkowitz Delta

Yosef Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz – the principals of the Applicant – through an
affiliated entity, own and operate AdviniaCare Pawtucket and AdviniaCare Providence. The Rhode
Island Department of Health (“RIDOH”) approved the CEC applications for the operations of those
facilities on January 31, 2025. In fact, an affiliated entity began providing management services at
those facilities pursuant to a RIDOH-approved management agreement since February of 2023. Since
their management of those facilities, the annual survey outcomes for the facilities significantly
improved, the operators prioritized decreasing turnover in key positions, the operators were able to
eliminate all agency staff and worked collaboratively with the unions in those facilities, and have
infused capital into the facilities. The Applicant will provide the same dedication to this Facility upon
approval of the CEC Application.

Moreover, Mr. Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz own and/or operate a total of 111
licensed facilities in 8 states.

Ben Berkowitz is an owner operator of 11 nursing facilities and senior housing facilities in Florida
and Massachusetts, as well as an investor in facilities in other states, Specifically, he is the Chief
Executive Officer of Pointe Group Care, LLC (“PGC”), which is headquartered in Massachusetts.
PGC employs staff focusing on operations, accounting, clinical, business development, technology
and accounts receivable and payable. PCG takes pride in providing high quality short-term
rehabilitation, nursing, and long-term care.

David Berkowitz and Yosef Meystel are the founders of Aperion Care, Inc. (“Aperion Care”).
Aperion Care is an administrative and management company firm that partners with geriatric
healthcare facilities. It specifically provides management services to skilled nursing facilities and
assisted living communities throughout Illinois and Indiana. Mr. Meystel began his career in
healthcare as an Assistant Administrator at Brightview Care Center in Chicago, Illinois. Following
Brightview, Mr. Meystel was the Administrator for EMI/EKS Management, where he became the
Administrator for Emerald Park Health Care Center. In 2006, Mr. Meystel founded YAM
Management, LLC and in 2014 formed Aperion Care, Inc., for which he serves as a board member
and shareholder. Aperion Care and PCG are now subsidiaries of the Kesser Group.

David Berkowitz serves as the President of Aperion Care, Inc., as well as a director and a shareholder.
He began his career in healthcare in 2002 as an administrator in training at Sebos Nursing & Rehab.
David Berkowitz then served as an administrator at a number of other skilled nursing facilities. He
has ownership interest in the real estate and/or operating entities of many skilled nursing facilities

                                           Appendix C (CONT.)

5.     Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and
operational policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services, and
accommodations, and a sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the proposal would
advance these areas:

a.     Resident’s physical environment:

      i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

       The facility offers both shared and private accommodations for residents. Common areas are
       available for interaction with other residents when preferred.

     ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

       The facility offers rooms with modern décor. The residential rooms can be decorated with the
       residents’ personal belongings to promote a more familiar and comfortable environment.

     iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s), laundry,
         activities;

       Laundry service is provided. The Applicant will offer a diverse nutritious menu that caters to
       personal preference, allergy needs, religious beliefs, and physical comfort. Group activities are
       available daily.

     iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and gardening);

       The facility offers many outdoor spaces, including, for example, a patio area.

b.     Resident-centered systems of care:

      i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and negotiated risk;

       The Facility offers a home-like and autonomous environment, while still maintaining
       appropriate physical security systems. The Applicant will ensure that the physical security
       system, including wander management systems on main exits and alarms on egress doors are
       current and operational.

     ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);

       The Applicant works with residents to schedule their preferred times for waking, bathing, and
       going to bed. The residents are also able to schedule their daily activities throughout the day.

     iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);



                                                          24

===== PAGE 163 =====
       The Applicant encourages the residents to provide their preferred dining time and location,
       as well as their meal preferences. Applicant will provide an alternate meal choice and make
       snacks available throughout the day. The dietary staff also ensures that residents with
       restrictive diets are able to enjoy an assortment of different meals.

     iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

       As set forth above, the structured recreational program includes a wide variety of activities
       for residents. The Applicant encourages resident feedback on those activities so that they can
       consistently improve and update the offerings. Residents may also participate in their own
       self-directed activities and always have access to television, books, movies, card games,
       beauty/barber salon and religious services for many denominations.

c.     Workforce administration:

      i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident services and
        foster relationship building?

       The Applicant will ensure that the facility maintains appropriate staffing ratios on all shifts
       and in all units. Staffing assignments take into account staff capabilities and specific needs of
       residents. In order to ensure the appropriate coverage, the Applicant continuously monitors
       the census and the residents’ conditions.

     ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g. Registered nurses,
        Licensed Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

       The Applicant will minimize staff turnover through job satisfaction and financial incentives.
       Staff is encouraged to recognize the significant role that they play in each residents’ life. Any
       changes in staffing are discussed with the residents before implementation.

20.      MULTI-EMPLOYER PENSION PLANS.

         With respect to each Multiemployer Pension Plan to which Sellers are obligated to
         contribute with respect to a Facility as disclosed on Schedules 18(o) and 18(x), the parties
         intend to comply with section 4204(a)(1) of ERISA, and to take any other action necessary
         or desirable, so that no liability is imposed upon APA Seller, Sellers or any affiliate thereof
         pursuant to Title IV of ERISA, as amended by the Multiemployer Pension Plan
         Amendments Act (“MPPAA”)(such liability hereinafter referred to as “Withdrawal
         Liability”) as a result of the consummation of the transactions contemplated herein or any
         subsequent action or omission of APA Purchasers, Purchasers or any affiliate thereof. To
         that end, the parties agree that:

                     i.   As of the Closing Date, Purchasers shall be obligated to contribute and shall
                          contribute to each Multiemployer Pension Plan with respect to the Facility
                          for the plan year of each Multiemployer Pension Plan in which the Closing
                          Date occurs and the subsequent five plan years for substantially the same
                          number of contribution base units (as defined in section 4001(a)(11) of
                          ERISA) for which Sellers had an obligation to contribute to such
                          Multiemployer Pension Plan in respect of the respective Facility prior to the
                          Closing Date.

                    ii.   Purchasers shall timely provide to each Multiemployer Pension Plan, at
                          their sole cost and expense, for the first plan year of the Multiemployer
                          Pension Plan beginning after the Closing Date and for each of the four (4)
                          plan years thereafter, a bond, escrow, letter of credit or other security that is
                          acceptable to the Multiemployer Pension Plan (a “Bond/Escrow”) that
                          complies with section 4204(a)(1)(B) of ERISA, in an amount equal to the
                          greater of:

                              -the average annual contribution required to be made by the Seller with
                              respect to the Facility to the Multiemployer Pension Plan for the three
                              (3) plan years preceding the plan year of the Multiemployer Pension
                              Plan in which the Closing Date occurs, or

                              -the annual contribution required to be made by the Seller with respect
                              to the respective Facility to the Multiemployer Pension Plan for the last
                              plan year of the Multiemployer Pension Plan completed before the plan
                              year of the Multiemployer Pension Plan in which the Closing Date
                              occurs;

22.     EVENTS OF DEFAULT; TERMINATION RIGHTS; REMEDIES. The breach by
either party (“Defaulting Party”) hereto of any term, provision, condition, promise, covenant,
agreement, representation, warranty, guaranty, indemnity, duty or obligation if not cured within
ten (10) business days of the earlier of said Defaulting Party’s receipt or refusal of written notice
of the same from the other party (“Non-Defaulting Party”) hereto shall automatically and without
further notice hereunder be an immediate event of default (“Event of Default”). It shall also be an
Event of Default if either Sellers or Purchasers are unable to meet a condition precedent prior to
the applicable date set forth herein for completion of such condition precedent that has not been
(A) waived in writing by the other party or (B) cured by the applicable party within ten (10) days
after written notice of such breach (except for the obligation to consummate the transactions
contemplated hereunder for which not notice or cure period shall be required and the same shall
be an immediate Event of Default). Upon an Event of Default hereunder by the Sellers, the
Purchasers shall be entitled to terminate this Agreement, whereupon APA Purchasers shall be
entitled to the return of the Deposit under the APA, and upon payment of such amount, this
Agreement shall terminate and be of no further force or effect, except as otherwise set forth herein.
Alternatively, Purchasers may pursue specific performance. Upon an Event of Default hereunder
by the Purchasers, the Sellers shall have the right to terminate this Agreement and APA Seller
under the APA shall have the right to retain the Deposit under the APA as liquidated damages.
Notwithstanding anything contained herein to the contrary, under no circumstances shall Sellers
or Purchasers be entitled to consequential, special, or punitive damages for a default by the other
hereunder. The provisions of this Section 22 shall survive the Closing Date or the earlier
termination of this Agreement.

Waterview Seller, and Summit Seller, collectively, “Seller” and each a “Seller”), and

Grove Buyer”), TRIPPS LANE, LLC (“Orchard View Buyer”), 99 HILLSIDE, LLC (“Summit

liability company (collectively “Purchaser”), and it’s permitted assigns pursuant to the terms
hereof (collectively, “Purchasers” and together with Seller, collectively, the “Parties” and each a
“Party”).

         A.    Orchard View Seller owns that certain 166 bed nursing facility commonly known
as “Orchard View Manor” located at 135 Tripps Lane, East Providence, RI 02915 (“Orchard View
Facility”). Heatherwood Seller owns that certain 114 bed nursing facility commonly known as

RI 02840 (the “Heatherwood Facility”). Waterview Seller owns that certain 132 bed nursing
facility commonly known as “Waterview Villa Rehabilitation & Skilled Care Center” located at
1275 South Broadway, East Providence, RI 02914 (the “Waterview Facility”). Summit Seller
owns that certain 165 bed nursing facility commonly known as “Summit Commons Rehabilitation
& Health Center” located at 99 Hillside Avenue, Providence, RI (Unit 1) 02906 (the “Summit
Facility”). Oakland Grove Seller owns that certain 165 bed nursing facility commonly known as
“Oakland Grove Health Care Center” located at 560 Cumberland Hill Road, Woonsocket, RI
02895 (the “Oakland Grove Facility”, and together with the Orchard View Facility, Heatherwood
Facility, Waterview Facility, Summit Facility, collectively are hereafter referred to as “Facilities”
and each individually, a “Facility).

       B.     Seller owns the land on which the Facilities are located, which is legally described
on Exhibit A-1 through A-5, attached hereto and made a part hereof. The “Land” shall be the
land described on Exhibits A-1 through A-5 and comprising the Facility, together with all
easements, hereditaments, privileges and appurtenances appurtenant thereto and belonging to
Seller. The “Improvements” shall be the buildings and improvements located on the Land,
including the Facilities, patios, courtyards, fences, parking areas and storage structures. The
“FF&E” shall be the furniture, fixtures, equipment and systems located in the Improvements and
owned by Seller.

       C.     Seller desires to sell and transfer the Property (as defined in Section 2) to Purchasers
and Purchasers desire to purchase the Property from the Seller.

         pursuant to the terms of the OTA (the “Personal Property”). The Personal Property shall
         include any personal property owned by third party vendors and leased to Seller as set forth
         on Schedule 3(e), attached hereto and made a part hereof (the “Leased Property”).

         c.      Intangible Property. The intangible property being assigned, set over and
         transferred by Seller to Purchasers shall consist of the following not otherwise assigned to
         New Operators pursuant to the terms of the OTA, all to the extent assignable any special
         use permits from the cities in which the Facilities are located (collectively the “Intangible
         Property”).

   following shall be excluded from the sale by Seller to Purchasers hereunder (the “Excluded

                    a.      Purchaser shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for any reason,

         the actual number of days in the month and a 365 or 366 day year, as the case may be. In
         connection with the foregoing, the parties agree to make the following apportionments:

                 (i)     Real estate taxes, assessments, personal property taxes, and water, vault and
         sewer charges and rents, as well as any other governmental charges or taxes assessed on

         which the prorations are based as a result of a tax complaint, revaluation or otherwise. This
         obligation to re-prorate shall survive the Closing. Allocation of real estate taxes billed with
         respect to the Property to yearly periods shall be determined in accordance with local
         custom, as determined by the Title Company. If, prior to the Closing, the Property or any
         portion thereof shall be affected by any special or general assessments which are or may
         become payable in installments, Seller shall (i) so inform Purchaser and (ii) pay the unpaid
         installments of such assessments which are due prior to the Closing and Purchaser shall
         pay the installments which are due on or after the Closing, but only to the extent those
         installments are attributable to the time period on or after the Closing.

                 (ii)    All charges and payments for utility services; provided, however, that if
         there is no meter or if the current bill for any of such utilities has not been issued prior to
         the Closing Date, then such charges shall be adjusted at the Closing on the basis of the
         charges for the prior period for which bills were issued and shall be further adjusted when
         the bills for the current period are issued; provided, further, to the extent possible, Seller
         shall terminate its accounts with the utility service providers and Purchaser shall establish
         its accounts with such utility service providers effective on the Closing Date, in which
         event, there shall be no proration for such utility services

                 (iii) Except as expressly provided herein, the purpose and intent as to the
         provisions of prorations and apportionments set forth in this Section and elsewhere in this
         Agreement is that Seller shall bear all expenses and liability of ownership and operation of

         and receive all such income accruing thereafter. Any other costs or charges of closing this

9. TITLE

         a.     Title to the Property at the Closing shall be good, marketable, fee simple title free
         and clear of all liens, encumbrances and easements affecting title except for the Permitted
         Encumbrances (as defined herein) and those which are permitted as provided in this
         Section.

         b.       Purchaser shall obtain a written title insurance commitment (the “Title
         Commitment”) from the Title Company. Purchaser shall have until 5:00 PM EST on the
         day that is ten (10) days after receipt of the Title Commitment but not later than the Due
         Diligence Expiration Date (the “Title Date”) to notify Seller, in writing, of the existence of
         any encumbrances and defects in title which are not excepted in this Agreement (the “Title
         Notice”) other than the Permitted Encumbrances, subject however to this Section. If
         Purchaser fails to deliver a Title Notice to Seller on or before 5:00 P.M. EST on the Title
         Date, then (i) this contingency shall be deemed to be of no further force or effect and (ii)
         all of the matters of record as of the Title Date shown on the Title Commitment (other than
         Seller’s Monetary Liens (as hereinafter defined), which Seller’s Monetary Liens Seller
         shall be responsible for paying and having released) shall be deemed to be “Permitted
         Encumbrances” as defined above. If, after giving the Title Notice to Seller, Purchaser
         learns, through continuation reports, title updates or other written evidence, of any title
         defects that Purchaser objects to or subject to which Purchaser believes it is not required to
         accept title, Purchaser shall give written notice thereof to Seller within ten (10) Business
         Days after the date Purchaser learns of same, and Purchaser shall be deemed to have
         unconditionally waived any such matters as to which it fails to give such written notice to
         Seller within such ten (10) Business Day period. If Purchaser delivers a Title Notice to
         Seller on or before 5:00 P.M. EST on the Title Date, then Seller shall have a period of ten
         (10) Business Days following the receipt of the Title Notice (such period the “Title Cure
         Period”) to either cure such defects (with written notice delivered to Purchaser of Seller’s
         completion of such cure together with evidence of the same reasonably satisfactory to
         Purchaser) or to expressly agree in writing to cure such defects on or before the Closing
         hereunder (any such title matter which Seller agrees to cure on or before the Closing herein
         called, a “Seller’s Title Matter”). Seller shall have no obligation whatsoever to expend or
         agree to expend any funds to cure any title objection (other than the discharge of monetary
         liens voluntarily granted by Seller and mechanics liens encumbering the Property relating
         to work performed at the Real Property and any violations or penalties that can be
         discharged solely by the payment of a sum certain, all of which Seller shall be responsible
         for paying and having released of record at the Closing (all of the foregoing items set forth
         in this sentence herein collectively, the “Seller’s Monetary Liens”) and Seller’s Title
         Matters which Seller shall also be responsible for having released of record at the Closing
         and provide written evidence to Purchaser of such payment(s)). If, within the Title Cure
         Period, Seller does not either cure such title objections set forth in the Title Notice (with
         written notice delivered to Purchaser of Seller’s completion of such cure together with
         evidence of the same reasonably satisfactory to Purchaser) and/or expressly agree in
         writing to cure such title defects on or before the Closing, then (x) Purchaser may thereupon
         elect to terminate this Agreement and receive a return of the Deposit or (y) Purchaser may
         accept such title as Seller is able to convey and otherwise subject to the remaining terms
         of this Agreement. If Seller does not expressly agree in writing to cure such title defects

         on or before the Closing, then Seller shall be deemed to have not agreed to cure such title
         defects. If Purchaser elects to terminate this Agreement pursuant to this Section, Purchaser

17. CASUALTY/CONDEMNATION.

         a.      Seller shall promptly notify Purchasers of any casualty damage it becomes aware
         of at any Facility or notice of condemnation that Seller receives prior to the Closing Date.

         b.      If: (A) any portion of the Property is damaged by fire or casualty after the Effective
         Date and is not repaired and restored substantially to its original condition prior to Closing,
         and (B) at the time of Closing the estimated cost of repairs is Two Hundred Thousand
         Dollars ($200,000.00) or less, as determined by an independent adjuster, Purchasers shall
         be required to purchase the Property in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and
         at Seller’s option, Purchasers shall either: (x) receive a credit at Closing of the estimated
         cost of repairs as determined by the aforesaid independent adjuster; or (y) at Closing Seller
         shall: (1) assign to Purchasers, without recourse, the right to all insurance claims and
         proceeds with respect thereto (less sums theretofore expended in connection with such fire
         or casualty, if any, by Seller, including for temporary repairs or barricades) (in which event
         Purchasers shall have the right to participate in the adjustment and settlement of any
         insurance claim relating to said damage), and (2) credit Purchasers at Closing with an
         amount equal to Seller’s insurance deductible.

         c.      If, prior to Closing, a “material” portion of the Property is taken by eminent domain,
         then Purchasers shall have the right within fifteen (15) days after receipt of notice of such
         material taking, to terminate this Agreement and the Deposit shall be returned to
         Purchasers. If Purchasers elect to proceed and to consummate the purchase despite said
         material taking (such election being deemed to have been made unless Purchasers notifies
         Seller to the contrary within fifteen (15) days after notice from Seller to Purchasers of any
         taking), or if there is less than a material taking prior to Closing, there shall be no reduction
         in or abatement of the Purchase Price and Purchasers shall be required to purchase the
         Property in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, and Seller shall assign to
         Purchasers, without recourse, all of Seller’s right, title and interest in and to any award
         made or to be made in the eminent domain proceeding (in which event Purchasers shall
         have the right to participate in the adjustment and settlement of such eminent domain
         proceeding). For the purpose of this Section, the term “material” shall mean any taking in
         excess of ten percent (10%) of the square footage of any Facility or twenty percent (20%)

         a means of egress and ingress to a public highway; or cause the use of the Facility after
         said taking to no longer be in compliance with all applicable zoning and building rules,
         regulations and ordinances.

shall have the meaning ascribed to them in the APA); and

        WHEREAS, the APA provides, inter alia, that Assignor shall assign to Assignee, Assignor’s

APA;

        NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and other good and valuable
consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, Assignor hereby agrees as

       1.       Transfer of Intangible Property. Assignor hereby assigns, sets over and transfers to
Assignee all of Assignor’s right, title and interest in, to and under all Intangible Property, to the extent the
same are assignable by Assignor.

         2.      Assumption. Assignee hereby accepts the foregoing assignments set forth above
provided, that said assignment and assumption shall in all respects be subject to the terms of the APA
with regard to the rights and obligations of each of the parties hereto with respect to the items assigned
hereunder, and in the event that any term of this Assignment shall contradict the APA, the APA shall
control.

         3.      Miscellaneous. This Assignment and the obligations of Assignor and Assignee
hereunder shall survive the closing of the transactions referred to in the APA shall be binding upon and
inure to the benefit of Assignor and Assignee, and their respective successors and assigns, shall be
governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Connecticut and may not be
modified or amended in any manner other than by a written agreement signed by the party to be charged
therewith.

===== PAGE 293 =====
                               Tab 18 - Charity Care Policy & Application



Purpose:

It shall be the policy of AdviniaCare Newport, LLC to provide free care to Residents on a case-by-
case basis, based on facility financial ability.
Qualifying Residents:
Provider will provide free care to those Residents who have a medical need for Provider's services
and who meet the charity care guidelines as outlined herein ("Qualifying Residents"). Accordingly,
Qualifying Residents will be those uninsured or underinsured Residents with incomes up to 125% of
the Federal Poverty Limits and who are without readily available funds that could be used to pay for
their care. (Qualifying Residents must have applied for any governmental assistance programs for
which they qualify. If a Qualifying Resident is not eligible for governmental assistance or is denied
governmental assistance, such Resident may apply for charity care.)
Charity Care Policy:
Provider agrees it will neither bill Qualifying Residents for services directly supplied by Provider nor
collect any fees for provision of such services. Services that are provided under contract with an
outside provider shall not be eligible for charity care and will be billed in the customary manner,
unless otherwise explicitly agreed to in writing by the outside provider.
Monitoring:
A summary of charity care provided will be drafted and provided to management on an annual basis.
